segments.title: 第35章 好看嗎?
segments.content:
Rekindling the Verdant Years Chapter 35: Is It Any Good?

The morning had felt a little boring at first.

But after Xu Youyu joined in, in the blink of an eye, it was already noon.

Li Luo played the guitar and sang a few songs that Xu Youyu liked. The two of them sat and chatted, and the sun rose high into the sky.

It was only when Xu Youyu's stomach started to rumble that the two of them snapped back to reality.

Looking at Li Luo with some embarrassment, Xu Youyu blinked, glanced at the kitchen, and asked in a low voice, "Are you still cooking for lunch?"

"I could, but..."

"I get it!" Xu Youyu stood up from the sofa. "I'll go buy groceries."

"No, no, no." Li Luo quickly stopped her, then got up and walked to the kitchen, opening the fridge to take a look. "What I mean is, there's some leftover rice from last night. If you don't mind, we can just make some fried rice for lunch."

Hearing that she didn't have to go buy groceries, Xu Youyu immediately nodded repeatedly, "Okay, I'm not picky."

"Alright then, just wait. It'll be ready soon." Li Luo took out a small piece of leftover pork belly from the fridge, half a bag of corn kernels, bean sprouts, a carrot, and two sausages.

Seeing him getting busy, Xu Youyu originally planned to wait obediently in the living room. But after thinking about it, she felt a little bad, so she turned back midway and walked into the kitchen.

"What's wrong?" Li Luo picked up the kitchen knife, placed the pork belly on the cutting board, and quickly sliced it, then cut it into shreds. Noticing Xu Youyu come in, he couldn't help but ask.

"Is there anything I can help with?" Xu Youyu asked, peeking from behind Li Luo.

Today, Xu Youyu was wearing a slip dress, revealing a pair of fair, slender arms. Her chest elegantly filled out the top, making Li Luo pause his knife to avoid cutting his own fingers.

"Have you ever cooked at home before?"

"Does cooking rice count?"

"I guess that勉強 counts... but I won't need you for that today." Li Luo pointed at the leftover rice in the rice cooker. He then thought for a moment and said, "Then help me wash the bean sprouts and the carrot, and unwrap the sausages."

"Okay, no problem!" Having been assigned a task, Xu Youyu was instantly full of energy and stood by the sink to start washing the vegetables.

As she washed, Xu Youyu secretly watched Li Luo chop the vegetables.

Having studied culinary arts for two and a half years at a vocational college, Li Luo's knife skills were quite impressive. The sound of his chopping was very rhythmic.

In Xu Youyu's memory, even when her mother chopped vegetables, she probably wasn't as fast or as fluid as Li Luo.

Watching Li Luo chop vegetables was truly a pleasant sight.

"You don't need to wash them for that long." Li Luo glanced at the vegetables in the sink and suddenly reminded her, "Just a quick rinse with water is fine."

"Oh, okay." Xu Youyu came back to her senses, quickly put the bean sprouts and carrot onto a plate, and handed it to Li Luo. Then she lowered her head and started unwrapping the sausages.

By the time she finished unwrapping them, Li Luo had already diced the carrot. He took the sausages from her, cut them on a diagonal into slices, set them aside, and then took out a small bowl to crack three eggs, whisking them evenly.

With that, the prep work was done.

"OK, thanks for your hard work." Li Luo clapped his hands and took the leftover rice out of the cooker. "You can leave the rest to me."

Xu Youyu stepped aside, watching as Li Luo skillfully added the prepared ingredients to the wok one by one. Steam filled the kitchen, and the aroma of rice began to spread.

She watched, somewhat mesmerized, her eyes on Li Luo's side profile as he seriously made fried rice. Certain notions swirled in her mind, finally coalescing into one thought—

Yes, I must write this scene into my book.

Just recently, she had been struggling with readers complaining that the daily interactions between her male and female leads lacked a sense of domestic warmth.

Xu Youyu thought to herself that she hadn't had the experience before, but now she had a ready-made source of inspiration. She'd like to see them say she lacked domestic warmth now!

As expected, when writing a book, one really had to draw more inspiration from life.

Thinking this, Xu Youyu found her gaze toward Li Luo growing more and more favorable.

Originally, she had been worried that after changing to a new landlord for her rented apartment, it would be difficult to get along, especially since she also had her two "kids" staying over.

But now, after spending a day together, the experience was far better than her previous rental.

When she first moved in last year, the other three rooms were all occupied by seniors in their third year of high school.

Everyone left early and returned late every day, silent and withdrawn. When they saw each other in the living room, they would just nod in acknowledgment, with no real friendship to speak of.

But now, with Li Luo and Ying Chanxi, not only did they have common topics to discuss, but there was also delicious food to eat.

Her quality of life had gone up a notch.

"Here, this is yours." Li Luo divided the fried rice onto two plates, then picked one up and headed toward the dining table in the living room.

Xu Youyu quickly picked up her plate and followed behind him.

"Senior Sister, are you staying here for the whole summer vacation? You didn't go home to live with your parents?" Li Luo casually tried to make conversation as they ate.

"I went back for a few days, then came back here." Xu Youyu chuckled. "When you first get home, everyone loves you. After a few days, even the dogs get tired of you."

"If you're in that state you were in this morning." Li Luo swallowed the rice in his mouth, paused for a second, "I can kind of understand your uncle and auntie."

Xu Youyu, who was busy eating, immediately stopped her chopsticks at his words and looked up at him. "...Don't think you can diss me like that just because you cooked for me. Don't your parents get tired of you?"

"Nope." Li Luo nodded. "My family runs a breakfast shop. After the summer vacation started, I woke up at three in the morning every day to go and help out. My parents couldn't bear to part with me."

Hit squarely by Li Luo's words, Xu Youyu was rendered speechless. She took a deep breath and gave him a thumbs-up.

However, after a few more bites of rice, Xu Youyu suddenly thought of something. Her eyes darted around, and she pulled her phone out of her pocket.

Li Luo glanced at the Apple phone Xu Youyu placed on the table and saw her unlock the screen, open the recently launched Qidian Reading app, and tap on a book that was very familiar to him.

Well... it was impossible not to be familiar with it.

After all, the book's title was "I'm Really Not a Superstar."

"Do you usually read novels?" Xu Youyu picked up her phone, waved it twice in Li Luo's direction, a mysterious smile on her face.

"I don't." Li Luo shook his head, his expression innocent. "I usually like to play games or watch anime."

It was better not to be too public about writing a novel.

Especially entertainment novels, which would more or less involve certain things between men and women. It would be a bit awkward if people he knew saw it.

The reason Li Luo had told his mom about it but not his dad was because his mom had a middle school education and most likely wouldn't read his book.

Even if she did, she would probably find it uninteresting after a chapter or two and wouldn't get to the parts that were unsuitable for an author's mother to see.

As for someone like Xu Youyu, who was a web novelist herself, it was even more important to keep it from her.

But at this moment, after hearing what Li Luo said, Xu Youyu sneered inwardly twice, thinking, *This kid is a pretty good actor.*

If her editor and Ying Chanxi hadn't both given her the same QQ number, Xu Youyu would never have guessed that Li Luo was the author of this book.

However, after his denial, Li Luo was still a little curious and couldn't help but ask, "What's that book you're reading about, Senior Sister? Is it any good?"
